content.text: The histogram reveals a **bimodal distribution**: the vast majority of points are near 0 (the cavity and exterior background) and a cluster near 1.0 (the solid sphere). Let me now find the spatial extent and probe along axes to locate the cavity precisely.

The NaN values suggest the grid goes from 0–99 but the data only covers part of it. The diagonal line may not pass through the cavity center. Let me probe along individual axes through the center of the solid sphere to find the cavity more precisely.

The data only goes up to x≈63 (after that it's NaN). The line y=50, z=50 is entirely zero — the solid sphere is not at that location. The grid seems to be non-square. Let me probe in different directions to understand the extent and find where the solid sphere actually lives.

The data is all zeros along z=0, y=0. The solid sphere must be in the interior. From the diagonal scan, I noticed the solid sphere (value=1) appeared around the middle of the diagonal. The dataset coordinates appear to be non-integer voxel indices. Let me probe through the center region that showed solid material in the diagonal scan.

Now I can see the solid sphere along x at y=30, z=30. The sphere goes from x≈11.3 to x≈53.0. The center along x is at (11.3+53.0)/2 ≈ 32.2. But crucially, I don't see any zero-gap INSIDE the sphere along this line — this means the cavity is not on the line y=30, z=30. The cavity must be off-center. Let me try probing through a different cross-section. From the diagonal scan, I saw zeros between samples 55-56 (x≈27-28) and 91-96 (x≈45-49). Let me search more systematically.

No cavity visible at y=25, z=35. The sphere exterior is at x≈12–52, centered around x≈32. Now I need to find the cavity. From the diagonal line, the cavity appeared at two locations. Let me understand: the diagonal showed zeros at about (27,27,27) and (45,45,45). Let me probe through those regions with a y-axis scan.

The sphere spans y≈10–53 at x=32, z=32. The center along y is at (10+53)/2 ≈ 31.5. No cavity visible at x=32, z=32. The solid sphere center appears to be around (32, 32, 32). The cavity must be offset from the center. Let me think about the diagonal scan result again.

From the diagonal (0,0,0)→(99,99,99) I saw zero dips at indices 53-56 (coords ~26-28) and 91-96 (coords ~45-49). These zeros within the otherwise solid sphere must be the cavity. The cavity appeared as a "tunnel" crossing the diagonal at two points, which is consistent with a spherical void — the diagonal passes through it entering and exiting. The midpoint of the zero region in the diagonal scan is the cavity center.

From the diagonal: zero gap between samples 54-56 (x≈26.7–27.7) and another gap at samples 91-96 (x≈45–49). Wait — those are TWO separate zero regions in the diagonal. Let me re-examine the diagonal data more carefully. At samples 53-56 (val≈0) and 91-96 (val≈0). These could be TWO separate cavities, or it could be the diagonal passes through the same cavity in two distinct segments (impossible for a convex cavity), or I'm misreading. Let me probe more carefully with targeted lines.

The sphere along z-axis at (32,32) spans z≈10–53, same as other axes. The sphere center is at (32, 32, 32) and it has a radius of about 21. No cavity is visible at the center — this confirms the cavity is offset from center.
